title: Maps On Maps
summary: Compares several place searches on one map. Alex rebuilt the 2016 web app as a cross-platform Expo and React Native app for iOS, Android, and web, using Google Places, Mapbox, and Apple MapKit behind a cost-limited Cloudflare Workers API. Alex also led the product and UI design, from AI-assisted prototypes to a shared design system with light and dark themes. Stack: Expo, React Native, TypeScript, Cloudflare Workers, Mapbox, Apple MapKit, and Google Maps. The iOS app is live on the App Store at https://apps.apple.com/us/app/maps-on-maps/id6823845844, and the web version is at https://mapsonmaps.com.

title: Reorder Nudge
summary: A Shopify app for wholesale (B2B) brands. It finds every B2B company in the store (or customers tagged wholesale), learns how often each shop usually reorders, flags the overdue and lapsed accounts, and drafts a reorder email listing their last order with a one-click cart link that rebuilds it. The merchant reviews and sends it from their own inbox. Free for up to 5 accounts, then $19 or $39 a month, billed through Shopify. Built as a React Router Shopify app. Site: https://reordernudge.com/.

title: Zombicide Weapon Odds
org: Personal project (designed and built by Alex)
summary: A web calculator for the Zombicide 2nd edition board game. Set two weapon loadouts side by side and see which is more likely to clear a zone in one attack. It covers every weapon in the core box, survivor skills, re-rolls (Plenty of Bullets, Plenty of Shells, Lucky), cars, and Molotovs, using binomial probability math. Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with light and dark themes. Live at https://alxdna.dev/zombicide/.

title: alxdna.dev
summary: Alex's portfolio site. Alex set the design direction and prototyped the site with AI design tools, then shipped it as a single static page with light and dark themes, a WebGL background, and alxdnAI, the self-hosted chat agent that answers questions about Alex's work.

title: alxdnAI
summary: Alex's hands-on AI agent work. Alex designed and built alxdnAI, the AI agent answering questions on alxdna.dev, as a production system: a TypeScript service on a free Oracle Cloud ARM VM runs an open-weights LLM (Qwen2.5 via Ollama) with no paid AI API. It uses tool calling to look up Alex's work instead of guessing, routes questions to the right tools, filters output so private details never leak, logs transcripts for review, and must pass a 31-case eval suite before each change. Alex used the evals to raise its pass rate from 63% to 100%.
